craft_claim: Reflective narration holds attention only while it keeps generating and answering causal, explanatory, and predictive questions; a reflective block that pauses the event-line without posing or advancing questions decays reader engagement — this is 'reflection that halts plot'.

supporting_evidence.note: Models narrative comprehension as the reader's construction of causal, explanatory, and predictive inferences; understanding-seeking (asking why/how/what-next) is a core motive, and comprehension proceeds where the text feeds those questions.

supporting_evidence.location: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 79(5):701-721; transportation construct, predictors, and persuasion results
supporting_evidence.note: Transportation — absorption in a narrative's events and imagery — predicts narrative persuasion and the felt experience of being lost in a text; its drivers are engagement with events and imagery, both of which interiority-only passages remove.

counterevidence.note: Transportation theory concerns narrative reading; the literary essay deliberately breaks transportation (Adorno: the essay's open, exploratory method), so in essay forms the mechanism shifts from event-momentum to question-momentum — the claim survives, its carrier changes.

scope: Narrative forms (fiction, memoir-in-scene, narrative blog) primarily; in essay forms apply the question-half of the mechanism only. Cross-links shared claims clm-pacing-rhythm-syntax and clm-point-of-view-psychic-distance.
exceptions: Diary, letter, and zuihitsu forms license longer event-free runs by reader contract; forward motion there is the advancing question or the dated entry, not the plot.
